title: The Strokes: The Band
description: Five New Yorkers in leather jackets who made rock cool again in 2001: the members, the albums and the stories.

cards.prompt: In which city did The Strokes form?
cards.details: The Strokes were so tied to downtown Manhattan that the city is practically a sixth member of the band.

cards.prompt: Who is The Strokes' singer and main songwriter?
cards.details: His lazy, deliberately distorted croon is one of the band's signature sounds.

cards.prompt: Which Strokes guitarist, known for his white Stratocaster, shares his name with his famous songwriter father?
cards.details: His dad, Albert Hammond, wrote "It Never Rains in Southern California".

cards.prompt: Who is The Strokes' other guitarist, famous for the intricate lead parts?
cards.details: The two-guitar interplay between Valensi and Hammond Jr., tight and interlocking with no flashy solos, defines the band's sound.

cards.prompt: Who plays bass in The Strokes?
cards.details: The quietest Stroke, with the steady, melodic basslines that hold the whole machine together.

cards.prompt: Who is The Strokes' drummer?
cards.details: Known for metronome-tight, almost drum-machine-like playing that gives the songs their propulsive feel.

cards.prompt: At which Swiss boarding school did Julian Casablancas and Albert Hammond Jr. first meet?
cards.details: One of the world's most famous (and expensive) boarding schools. They reconnected years later in New York.

cards.prompt: Julian Casablancas' father founded which famous modelling agency?
cards.details: John Casablancas founded Elite, one of the biggest modelling agencies of the supermodel era.

cards.prompt: What is The Strokes' 2001 debut album?
cards.details: Eleven songs in about 36 minutes. Often called one of the defining albums of the decade. No question mark in the title!

cards.prompt: Who produced Is This It?
cards.details: Recorded in a small Manhattan basement studio. The raw, compressed sound was a deliberate choice.

cards.prompt: Which British indie label released Is This It in the UK?
cards.details: The band broke in the UK first, where the music press went wild for them before America caught on.

cards.prompt: Which song was removed from the US release of Is This It after the September 11 attacks?
cards.details: It was replaced by "When It Started". The original UK version kept it.

cards.prompt: The US cover of Is This It replaced the UK cover's provocative photo with an image of what?
cards.details: The UK cover showed a gloved hand on a bare hip. The US version swapped it for colourful subatomic particle tracks from a bubble chamber.

cards.prompt: Which Is This It single became The Strokes' breakthrough hit in 2001?
cards.details: Spelled "Nite". One of the songs that defined early-2000s indie rock.

cards.prompt: Which nostalgic Is This It single shares its name with a word for "at some point in the future"?
cards.details: A breezy, bittersweet song about friendship, and one of the band's most loved.

cards.prompt: The Strokes helped lead the early-2000s revival of which rock style?
cards.details: Along with bands like The White Stripes and Yeah Yeah Yeahs, they made scrappy guitar bands huge again.

cards.prompt: Which music magazine named Is This It the best album of the 2000s?
cards.details: The British weekly championed the band from their very first EP.

cards.prompt: What is The Strokes' 2003 second album?
cards.details: Made quickly after the debut's success, and it sounds like a slightly sharper, slicker sequel.

cards.prompt: What was the lead single from Room on Fire, named after a time on the clock?
cards.details: Known for a guitar part that sounds more like a synthesizer than a guitar.

cards.prompt: Which Room on Fire single is named after a class of animals including lizards and snakes?
cards.details: A fan favourite. Its tense, driving riff is a staple at Strokes shows.

cards.prompt: What is The Strokes' 2006 third album?
cards.details: Longer, louder and more polished than the first two, with a more mixed reception at the time.

cards.prompt: Which heavy, bass-driven single led First Impressions of Earth?
cards.details: A big change from the earlier sound, with a snarling bass riff out front.

cards.prompt: What is The Strokes' 2011 fourth album?
cards.details: Their first album after a five-year gap, and the first with songwriting spread across the band.

cards.prompt: What is The Strokes' 2013 fifth album?
cards.details: Synthy and falsetto-heavy. The band did very little promotion for it.

cards.prompt: What is The Strokes' 2020 album, which won a Grammy?
cards.details: It won Best Rock Album, the band's first Grammy, nearly 20 years after their debut.

cards.prompt: Which famous producer worked with The Strokes on The New Abnormal?
cards.details: The co-founder of Def Jam, who has produced everyone from the Beastie Boys to Johnny Cash.

cards.prompt: Which song opens The New Abnormal?
cards.details: A smooth, wistful opener that many fans count among their best songs.

cards.prompt: Which New Abnormal closing track is named after a New York baseball team?
cards.details: A melancholy, sweeping goodbye to an era. The perfect closer.

cards.prompt: "Bad Decisions" borrows its melody from which Billy Idol song?
cards.details: The borrowing is so clear that Billy Idol and Tony James got songwriting credits.

cards.prompt: What is Julian Casablancas' experimental side band called?
cards.details: Much noisier and weirder than The Strokes. Casablancas uses it to chase stranger sounds.

cards.prompt: Which breezy side project did drummer Fabrizio Moretti form with Rodrigo Amarante?
cards.details: A sunny, bossa-nova-tinged band. About as far from The Strokes' edge as you can get.

cards.prompt: What was Albert Hammond Jr.'s 2006 debut solo album?
cards.details: He was the first Stroke to go solo, with brighter, poppier songs.
